finding: the firmware writes META TXDIVTIME (CT.28, 0x048000e0) = 1, the default and 'maximum resolution' (upstream metag_regs.h: DIV 1..256, 'timers run at 1 MHz @1/1')

the same init function (0x100209b4) arms thread 0's TXTIMER (0x04800020) with the complement of (period x 1000 >> 8) before the loop runs. Request 23 said it was not armed before the first sleep; that was wrong

period = priv +0x270 (or +0x2c4 when the sampler gate is on). The init copy fills priv +0x270 from config +0x2a8, the perf table's second MHz entry (365 for state 1 in blob f's E2 table); priv +0x2c4 is set later by the governor (0x1001b624/0x1001b6b4). So the tick is derived from the GPU clock of the current perf state, about 1 ms if the timer counts at core clock / 256 (inferred)
the TXTIMER tick needs META's core or timer clock running. A 30 s silence (run 77) means META's clock is not running, or META is held, rather than a wrong timer setting (inferred)
the timer tick, the MTS trigger and slave-port service all stop at once if the GPU or META clock stops after the firmware goes idle. That is one cause for all three symptoms (inferred)

Orchard's ~290 alive records a second is the A9 firmware's scheduler pass rate; the J81 loop posts alive once per entry (request 22), so the count does not compare directly. The A9 docs here name no host-programmed timer or interrupt path for META
the AIC lines (134-138, the firmware's is 138) are firmware-to-host only. Apple's host unmasks AIC 0x86/0x87/0x8a after boot (request 17); nothing on the AIC side feeds META
